docs.title: Welcome to Sia AI Documentation
docs.text: Sia AI is a powerful business intelligence (BI) platform that allows you to interact with your data using natural language. This documentation will guide you through its core components and teach you how to leverage its features for effective data analysis.

docs.title: Core Components Overview
docs.text:
Sia AI is composed of several key components that work together to turn your natural language questions into data visualizations and insights.

Component Role Description Chat Interface Primary User Interaction The main page where you ask questions in plain English. The AI interprets your prompt, generates a SQL query, executes it, and returns a chart or data table. Modeling Page Semantic Layer Definition This is where you define the "business logic" of your data. You can define models (tables), relationships between them, custom metrics, and calculated fields. This provides the AI with the necessary context about your data schema. Knowledge Base Context Enrichment A repository for business-specific terms, definitions, and synonyms. This helps the AI understand your organization's unique vocabulary, like "What is our ARR?" or "Show me our top-performing SKUs." SQL Change Component Correction & Refinement A powerful feature that allows you to directly view and edit the SQL query generated by the AI. This is essential for correcting mistakes and fine-tuning complex analyses. Views & Dashboards Persistence & Sharing Allows you to save frequently used queries as "Views" and pin insightful charts to create shareable "Dashboards" for monitoring key metrics.

docs.title: How They Fit Together: The Workflow
docs.text:
1. Modeling: An administrator or data analyst first uses the Modeling Page to define the semantic layer over the raw database tables. This is a one-time setup (with ongoing maintenance) that tells WrenAI how your data is structured (e.g., users table joins to orders table on user_id).
  2. Enriching Context: The Knowledge Base is populated with business terms. For example, you can define "Active User" as a user who has logged in within the last 30 days.
  3. Asking Questions: A user goes to the Chat Interface and asks a question like, "Show me the number of active users per month."
  4. AI Interpretation: Sia AI's LLM uses the context from the Modeling Page and the Knowledge Base to translate the user's question into a precise SQL query.
  5. Execution & Visualization: The SQL query is run against the database, and the results are displayed as a chart or table.
  6. Refinement: If the AI makes a mistake, the user can use the SQL Change Component to correct the query. The user can then save this corrected logic as a View or add a term to the Knowledge Base to improve future performance.
  7. Dashboarding: If the resulting chart is valuable, the user can pin it to a Dashboard for easy access later.

docs.title: Configuring Language Models
docs.text: As an administrator, you can configure Sia AI to use different large language models (LLMs) as its core engine. This allows you to switch between providers like OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, or even use a self-hosted model, depending on your organization's performance, cost, and security requirements.

docs.title: Locating the Configuration File
docs.text:
The LLM configuration is managed in the main configuration file for the Sia AI application.

  • File Location: The file is named config.yaml and is typically located in the root directory of your Sia AI installation.

Backup Before Editing

Always create a backup of your config.yaml file before making any changes. An incorrect configuration can prevent the application from starting.

docs.title: Syntax for LLM Configuration
docs.text: Inside config.yaml, you will find a section dedicated to the language model, usually under a key like llm or model_provider. You need to specify the provider and provide the necessary credentials.

docs.title: Example 1: Using OpenAI (GPT-4)
docs.text:
To use an OpenAI model, you need to provide the model name and your API key.

# config.yaml

llm:
  provider: openai
  config:
    model: "gpt-4-turbo"
    api_key: "sk-YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY" # It is highly recommended to use an environment variable instead

# config.yaml


llm:
  provider: google
  config:
    model: "gemini-1.5-pro-latest"
    api_key: "YOUR_GOOGLE_AI_STUDIO_API_KEY" # Use environment variables for production

# config.yaml

llm:
  provider: openai # Many local servers use an OpenAI-compatible API
  config:
    model: "llama3-70b" # The name of the model served by your local endpoint
    api_base: "http://localhost:8000/v1" # The base URL of your local LLM server
    api_key: "not-needed" # API key can often be a dummy string for local models

docs.title: Creating Dashboards
docs.text: Dashboards in Sia AI allow you to collect and display multiple charts in a single view. They are perfect for monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs) and sharing insights with your team.

docs.title: Workflow for Creating a Dashboard
docs.text: Creating a dashboard is a straightforward process that starts from the chat interface.

docs.title: Step 1: Generate a Chart
docs.text:
First, use the chat interface to ask a question and generate a chart that you find valuable.

Example Prompt: Show me our weekly revenue for the last 90 days as a bar chart.

docs.title: Step 2: Pin the Chart
docs.text: Once the chart is generated and you are satisfied with it, locate the "Pin to Dashboard" button (often represented by a thumbtack icon 📌) above the chart area.

docs.title: Step 3: Add to a Dashboard
docs.text:
Clicking the "Pin to Dashboard" button will open a dialog box with two options:

  1. Add to Existing Dashboard: A dropdown menu will list all existing dashboards. Select the one where you want to add your chart.
  2. Create New Dashboard: If you want to start a new dashboard, select this option and give your new dashboard a descriptive name (e.g., "Q3 Sales Performance").

### Step 4: View and Arrange Your Dashboard

  • Navigate to the "Dashboards" section from the main navigation menu.
  • Select the dashboard you just created or added to.
  • All your pinned charts will be displayed as widgets.
  • You can rearrange the widgets by dragging and dropping them, and resize them to create the perfect layout.

Build Dashboards Iteratively

You don't need to create all your charts at once. As you discover new insights through your conversations with Sia AI, you can continuously add them to relevant dashboards. This makes your dashboards a living reflection of your ongoing data analysis.

docs.title: The Chat Interface: Asking Questions
docs.text: The Home Page is your primary gateway to interacting with Sia AI. Its design is centered around a conversational experience, allowing you to ask questions about your data as if you were talking to a data analyst.

docs.title: Page Layout and Components
docs.text:
The chat interface is simple and intuitive, consisting of four main areas:

  1. Chat History (Left Sidebar): All your previous conversations are saved here. You can revisit, rename, or delete past chats.
  2. Prompt Input Bar (Bottom): This is where you type your questions (prompts) to the AI.
  3. Response Area (Center): The main content area where Sia AI displays its answers. This can be a data table, a chart, or a text-based answer.
  4. Interaction Tools (Above Response): After a response is generated, several tools appear:
    • Change SQL: View and edit the SQL query generated by the AI.
    • Change Chart Type: Switch between different visualizations (e.g., bar chart, line chart, pie chart).
    • Save to...: Save the query as a View or add context to the Knowledge Base.
    • Pin to Dashboard: Add the current chart to a new or existing dashboard.

docs.title: User Interaction Flow
docs.text:
Your workflow on the chat page typically follows these steps:

  1. Ask an Initial Question: Start by typing a clear question into the prompt input bar. For example: What were our total sales last quarter?
  2. Review the Response: Sia AI will process your request and generate a response, usually a chart or a number.
  3. Ask Follow-up Questions: You can continue the conversation to refine your analysis. The AI remembers the context of the current chat. For example:
    • Break that down by product category.
    • Now show it as a line chart.
    • Compare it to the same quarter last year.
  4. Refine or Correct: If the chart doesn't look right, use the Change SQL button to inspect and correct the underlying query.
  5. Save Your Work: Once you are satisfied with a chart or query, use the Pin to Dashboard or Save to View features to preserve your work.

Start Simple, Then Iterate

It's often best to start with a broad question and then ask follow-up questions to drill down into the details. This conversational approach is a strength of Sia AI.

docs.title: The Knowledge Base: Teaching WrenAI Your Business Language
docs.text: The Knowledge Base is a powerful feature that allows you to teach Sia AI the specific terminology, synonyms, and business logic unique to your organization. It acts as a centralized repository of contextual information that helps the AI better understand and respond to user prompts.

docs.title: Purpose of the Knowledge Base
docs.text:
Databases have technical names (fct_transactions, dim_users), but your team uses business terms ("revenue," "customers," "ARR"). The Knowledge Base bridges this gap.

Use it to define:

  • Synonyms: Map common terms to your data model.
    • customers -> users model
    • revenue, sales, income -> total_price column in the orders model
  • Business Definitions: Store definitions for complex metrics or concepts. When a user asks "What is ARR?", the AI can retrieve the definition you've stored.
  • Common Filters: Define frequently used filters.
    • Term: Active Users
    • Mapping: users.last_login_date > DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)

docs.title: How to Add to the Knowledge Base
docs.text:
You can add entries to the Knowledge Base in two ways:

  1. Directly on the Knowledge Page:

    • Navigate to the "Knowledge" section from the main menu.
    • Click "Add New Entry."
    • Enter the term (e.g., "Churned Customer").
    • Provide its definition or map it to a specific model, column, or SQL expression.

  2. From the Chat Interface (Save to Knowledge):

    • This is the most common and effective workflow.
    • After the AI successfully generates a chart based on a complex prompt, you can save the underlying logic.
    • For example, you ask: show me users who have not made a purchase in the last 6 months.
    • After Sia AI generates the correct list, click Save to... -> Save to Knowledge.
    • You can then map the term "Churned Customer" to the logic WrenAI just used. The next time someone asks for "churned customers," the AI will know exactly what to do.

The Knowledge Base is Proactive

Adding entries to the Knowledge Base is a proactive way to reduce errors and improve the accuracy of Sia AI for all users. Encourage your team to save common definitions and business logic whenever possible.

docs.title: The Modeling Page: Defining Your Data's Logic
docs.text: The Modeling Page is where you build the semantic layer that Sia AI uses to understand your database schema. By defining models, relationships, and custom fields, you provide the essential context the AI needs to write accurate SQL queries.

docs.title: What is Modeling?
docs.text:
In the context of Sia AI, "modeling" is the process of mapping your raw database tables and columns to business-friendly concepts. It's about adding a layer of meaning on top of your data.

A well-defined model allows users to ask questions using business terms (e.g., "revenue," "customers") instead of database terms (e.g., sum(order_items.sale_price), count(distinct users.id)).

docs.title: Key Modeling Concepts
docs.text:
The Modeling Page allows you to configure the following:

  • Models: A model is typically a direct mapping to a table or view in your database. You can select which tables to expose to Sia AI.
  • Columns: Within each model, you can manage its columns. You can rename them for clarity, hide them from the AI, or change their data type.
  • Relationships: This is where you define how models connect to each other. For example, you would define a many-to-one relationship from an orders model to a users model on the user_id column.
    • orders.user_id -> users.id
  • Calculated Fields: Create new columns using SQL expressions. This is perfect for defining custom metrics that don't exist in the database.
    • Example: Create a profit column in your orders model with the expression sale_price - cost.
  • Custom Metrics: Define aggregations that are frequently used.
    • Example: Create a metric called Average Order Value (AOV) with the expression AVG(total_price).

docs.title: How to Interact with the Modeling Page
docs.text:
1. Connect Your Data Source: The first step is to connect Sia AI to your data warehouse or database.
  2. Select Tables to Model: From the list of available tables, select the ones you want to expose to the AI. Sia AI will create a default model for each selected table.
  3. Define Relationships: Navigate to the "Relationships" tab. Click "Add Relationship" and define the connections between your models (e.g., join orders and products on product_id).
  4. Create Calculated Fields/Metrics: Go to a specific model and click "Add Calculated Field." Provide a user-friendly name and the SQL expression.

Accurate Relationships are Critical

The AI relies heavily on the defined relationships to correctly join tables. An incorrect or missing relationship is the most common cause of failed queries. Ensure your join keys and cardinality (one-to-one, many-to-one, etc.) are accurate.

docs.title: Effective Prompting & Data Analysis
docs.text: The quality of your input (the prompt) directly impacts the quality of Sia AI's output. Learning how to craft effective prompts and correct the AI when it makes mistakes is key to mastering the platform.

docs.title: Crafting Effective Prompts
docs.text:
Follow these best practices to get the most accurate results:

  1. Be Specific: Vague questions lead to vague answers.

    • Bad: Show me sales.
    • Good: Show me total sales revenue by month for the year 2024.

  2. Use Correct Terminology: Use the names of models, columns, and metrics as defined in the Modeling Page. If you've defined a metric called "Average Order Value," use that exact term.

  3. Request a Chart Type: You can guide the AI to the best visualization.

    • Show monthly active users as a line chart.
    • What is the breakdown of sales by region? Show it as a pie chart.

  4. Build on a Conversation: Use follow-up questions to drill down.

    • Q1: What are our top 5 selling products this year?
    • Q2 (Follow-up): For those products, what was the monthly sales trend?

docs.title: Correcting Mistakes with "Change SQL"
docs.text: Even with perfect prompting, the AI can sometimes misunderstand your intent or generate an incorrect SQL query. The Change SQL feature gives you full control to correct it.

docs.title: Example Scenario: Detecting and Correcting an Error
docs.text:
Let's say you want to find the number of distinct users who made a purchase each month.

  1. Your Prompt: Show me the number of users who made a purchase each month.
  2. AI's Interpretation: The AI might misinterpret this and count the total number of orders instead of distinct users. The resulting chart shows unusually high numbers.
  3. Detect the Mistake: The numbers look wrong. You suspect the AI counted transactions instead of users.
  4. Use "Change SQL":
    • Above the chart, click the Change SQL button.
    • A modal will appear with the generated SQL query. You might see something like this: 
      -- Incorrect Query
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month,
  COUNT(order_id) AS number_of_orders -- Mistake is here!
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
  5. Update the SQL: You can directly edit the query in the text box. You correct COUNT(order_id) to COUNT(DISTINCT user_id). 
    -- Corrected Query
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS number_of_distinct_users -- Corrected!
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
  6. Apply Changes: Click "Run Query." The chart will now update with the correct data based on your revised SQL.

docs.title: Improving Performance with Save Features
docs.text: After correcting a query, you can teach Sia AI to avoid making the same mistake in the future.

docs.title: Save to Knowledge
docs.text: If the correction involves a specific business term, use Save to Knowledge. - Scenario: You prompted for "user growth," and the AI counted all new user signups. You used Change SQL to define it as net user growth (new_signups - churned_users). - Action: Click Save to... -> Save to Knowledge. Define the term "User Growth" and associate it with your corrected logic. The next time anyone asks for "user growth," Sia AI will use the correct definition.

docs.title: Save to View
docs.text: If the query is complex and likely to be reused often, save it as a View. - Scenario: You've crafted a multi-join query to generate a complex "Daily Operations Report." - Action: After finalizing the query with Change SQL, click Save to... -> Save to View. Name it "Daily Operations Report." Now, users can simply prompt Show me the Daily Operations Report instead of typing the complex question again.
